newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Gwalia sees yr net earnings A$40 mln.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Gwalia sees yr net earnings A$40 mln.

text.p: Gold miner Sons of Gwalia Ltd said on Wednesday it anticipates recording net earnings of A$40 million in the 1996/97 (July-June) financial year.

"Based on current projections, the company anticipates gold production of approximately 530,000 fine ounces for the full year, which will include its attributable production from the Yilgarn Star and Nevoria mines in Western Australia and the Salsigne mine in France and net earnings of approximately $40 million," the company said in a statement accompanying its half year results.

A gold hedging programme would sustain profits and cash flows in the future and underwrite extensive capital and exploration programmes over the next few years in key regional gold belts, Sons of Gwalia said.
It said two million ounces, representing about 58 percent of current proved and probable ore reserves and 29 percent of combined reserves and resource had been sold forward.
As a result, gold production over the next few years would be sold at prices of between A$640 and A$660 an ounce.

Sons of Gwalia also said it did not intend to proceed at this stage with a proposed expansion of its Marvel Lock milling plant capabilities pending further investigation. The expansion would have increased throughput to 2.5 million tonnes a year from the current 1.9 million to 2.0 million tonnes.
"A new reserve and resource calculation will be completed before the end of the March quarter, which will assist in making this decision," it said.

Sons of Gwalia also said that it expects the Yilgarn Star, Sons of Gwalia and Laverton Mines to perform well in the second half but that the Bullfinch mine was expected to produce a lower-than-expected 95,000 ounces for the year due to lower grades and difficulties associated with mining contractors in the first quarter.
